findings.finding: Import statements are not hashed, aliases included, so a test can be pointed at another module (from . import scenario_support as oracle) without changing its hash; the meta import allow-list ignores asname.
findings.suggestion: Hash the import bindings of names in the closure and reject differing aliases. Recorded in FINDINGS for stop 2; the lock is not created in this campaign.

findings.finding: In the left_stale case the committed-versions check cannot tell a refused release commit from no release commit at all.
findings.suggestion: Assert the release commit subject or the exact committed map.

findings.finding: The AC11 aggregation-half test never calls the oracle although the docs say each promise test is judged through it.
findings.suggestion: Add an oracle function and check per test in the meta test.

findings.finding: covers_of reads pytestmark only from plain Assign, not AnnAssign or AugAssign.
findings.suggestion: Share one target-extraction helper.

findings.finding: Fingerprint uniqueness check keys by bare test name across two files.
findings.suggestion: Key by file::name.

findings.finding: Dead condition tag != v0.1.0.
findings.suggestion: Use if tag:.

findings.finding: Stand-in covers tags (AC14, AC01) inflate coverage counts.
findings.suggestion: Record as a stop-2 decision (done in FINDINGS).

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: A changed helper always changes the hash — A module-level rebinding after a def is ignored because the def wins in lookup.

Claim under doubt: Every fixture or hook that can affect a locked test is in its closure — Non-literal autouse, module-level pytest_generate_tests, parent conftests and golden/__init__.py are outside every closure and REQUIRED.
Claim under doubt: The hash is identical on Python 3.11 and 3.12 — No literal digest is pinned; f-string parsing changed in 3.12.
Claim under doubt: A rename is not a change of the promise — The fingerprint drops the test name.
Claim under doubt: The promise tests go red when the skill changes — AC04 lacks footer and chore cases, AC10 only dry-runs aggregation, AC11 aggregation half is a tautology.
Claim under doubt: The oracle field separates trace from test honestly — AC14 and AC15 page parts read the stub release state but are labelled test.
Claim under doubt: passing means the named test runs green — The meta test checks presence only.

The list's own definition of `oracle: trace` is "ONLY the replay's recorded stub state or log; such parts are their own entries". AC14's check (`test_ac14_...`) reads `s.gh_state()["releases"]` and AC15's main check reads `s.gh_state()["releases"]` — facts visible only in the stub — yet both entries are marked `oracle: "test"`, while AC01/request and AC15/no-backfill were split out precisely because they read the same stub. The classification is internally inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Either split the stub-visible halves of AC14/AC15 into their own `oracle: trace` entries (as done for AC01 and AC15/no-backfill), or re-word the note so the rule covers these entries; stop 2 should not have to guess which convention holds.

findings.finding: The test only inserts `shared/testkit` into `sys.path`; `ac_move_map` lives in `shared/scripts/lib`, so `from lib import ...` resolves only if some other conftest already puts `shared/scripts` on the path. Nothing in the diff guarantees that, and the mirror-parser test would error with ModuleNotFoundError rather than pin the parsers.
findings.suggestion: Insert `shared/scripts` into `sys.path` explicitly (or import via the same mechanism the rest of the suite uses for `lib`), and verify this test runs standalone.

findings.finding: _names` adds every function argument name to the lookup set, so a helper parameter that shadows a module-level constant or helper (e.g. `def helper(LIMIT):` while `LIMIT = 3` sits at module level) pulls the constant into the closure even though the helper shadows it. That is over-inclusion (hash churn on edits the test never observes), the opposite failure of the documented under-inclusion limits, and it is not documented as a known limit.
findings.suggestion: Exclude argument names from the module-level lookup when the name is bound locally in the same function (check `ast.Assign`/arg bindings per scope), or at minimum document the over-inclusion beside the other known limits.

findings.finding: Constant(value=None)` serializes as `{"_": "Constant"}` because the `None` field value is dropped. In the cases I traced (Compare ops, defaults, call args) the surrounding structure still distinguishes them, so there is no collision today — but it is fragile: any future AST position where a bare `Constant` is compared positionally (e.g. two `comparators` entries, one `None` one dropped-elsewhere) could collide. Worth a pinning test.
findings.suggestion: Add a test asserting `x is None` vs `x is not None`, `f(None)` vs `f(0)` and `def f(a=None)` vs `def f(a="")` all produce distinct normalized forms.

findings.finding: The test restates the `compare_runs.py` schema by hand (key presence + decision vocabulary) but the actual tool was never run, and the schema was read from `/tmp` copies. The unit's AC says scenarios.json "validates against it (a test loads and checks it)" — this satisfies the letter, but a schema drift in the real tool (e.g. a required field this restatement doesn't know) would not be caught until stop 2.
findings.suggestion: As the FINDINGS already ask, have stop 2 run the real `compare_runs.py` over the file; optionally record the tool's content hash in the file and fail if it changes.

findings.finding: The alignment rule says entries carry a "source anchor (file, heading path, content hash)". All non-spec entries have `content_hash: null`; the meta test even asserts `content_hash is None` for them. If the skill-check tool requires a hash string, every JUDGE and PROPOSED entry fails its validation at stop 2.
findings.suggestion: Compute a real content hash for the anchored heading text in `SKILL.md`/`release-workflow.md`, or get an operator answer on whether null is accepted before stop 2 tries to compare.  Overall: the unit is substantially complete against the spec (driver-only tests, six statuses, no 'uncovered', move-map resolution, nothing deleted), and the hashing helper is well-tested; the issues above are consistency and verification gaps rather than broken logic, but the AC14/AC15 oracle classification and the `from lib` import should be settled before stop 2 leans on this.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Module-level behavioral marks are excluded from the fingerprint. Adding `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip(reason="later")` leaves the hash unchanged, allowing a locked promise test to stop running without detection.
findings.suggestion: Include module-level behavioral marks in each test’s normalized fingerprint. Add regression tests for module-level `skip`, `xfail`, and `parametrize`.

findings.finding: Fixtures requested through `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("guard")` are not followed. The decorator is hashed, but `"guard"` is a string rather than an AST name, so changing or removing assertions inside that fixture leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Resolve fixture names from `usefixtures` arguments and fixture `name=` aliases, then include their dependency closures. Test that changing such a fixture changes the hash.

findings.finding: The closure deduplicates definitions by bare name across modules. If the test module and a supplied `conftest.py` both define `LIMIT`, a test using its own `LIMIT` and a conftest fixture using the other will include only one. Changes to the omitted constant will not change the fingerprint.
findings.suggestion: Track definitions by module identity and name, and resolve each dependency in its defining module. Add a test with colliding constants in the test module and conftest.

findings.finding: The source-anchor check explicitly requires non-spec content hashes to be `null`. Consequently, all judgement and proposed entries lack the content hash required by the specified anchor shape, and edits to their source text are undetected while the heading remains.
findings.suggestion: Populate hashes for those anchored source sections and validate them against normalized section content.  Ship-with-fixes: the promise tests and scenario artifacts largely follow the requested structure, but the hashing omissions undermine the lock’s central guarantee. Repository access was blocked, so this assessment is limited to the supplied diff and does not confirm test execution.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
